evidence.note: After finding /app empty, the agent codes app.py from scratch stating it will implement SigV4 verification, error codes, testid-driven console — driven by the spec's enumerated contract points rather than any probe of boto3/botocore signing internals. Shows recall of the broad contract but no active canonical-request capture.

boto3 round-trip smoke test REVEALS that boto3 generated a legacy SigV2 presigned query (AWSAccessKeyId/Signature/Expires) not SigV4 — a real-contract discovery made reactively via testing, then patched. Demonstrates understanding of the signing distinction but this contract detail was discovered during verification, not probed proactively.

Final submission summarizes the implemented surface; no systematic captured signing fixtures or a maintained inventory mapping every required behavior/error/testid — orientation stayed at spec-extraction plus round-trip smoke testing.

reasoning: The agent reliably extracted the concrete contract points from the spec (error codes, ETag rule, health endpoint, testid-driven console, audit semantics) and implemented SigV4 header signing from recalled knowledge — squarely matching the level-5 anchor. It went slightly beyond pure spec-reading by running boto3 round-trips that surfaced real contract subtleties (the SigV2-vs-SigV4 presign mismatch), but these were reactive verification discoveries, not the proactive botocore canonical-request capture or full testid/error-code enumeration the level-8 anchor describes, and there is no systematic captured-fixture reference. This places the observed behavior at the level-5 mark with only mild reach toward 6.
